articleBody:
A toilet overflow can quickly turn a normal day into a watery disaster in your Summerlin home. While emergencies happen, a lot of overflows are actually preventable with a little proactive care. This checklist is designed to help you keep your toilets running smoothly and avoid those stressful, messy situations.

How to use this checklist: Go through these points periodically, especially if you notice any small issues. Addressing minor problems early can save you from a major headache later.

- [ ] Teach household members about appropriate flushing — why it matters: Make sure everyone knows not to flush anything other than human waste and toilet paper. Wipes, feminine hygiene products, and excessive paper are common causes of clogs and overflows.
- [ ] Keep a plunger handy and know how to use it — why it matters: A good plunger can often clear minor clogs before they escalate. Make sure it forms a good seal over the drain for effective use.
- [ ] Check for a constantly running toilet — why it matters: A running toilet can indicate a faulty flapper or fill valve, which can contribute to weak flushes and potential overflows. It also wastes a lot of water.
- [ ] Inspect the toilet's shutoff valve periodically — why it matters: Ensure the valve behind the toilet turns freely. If an overflow occurs, you'll need to turn this off quickly, and a corroded or stuck valve can make the problem much worse by preventing you from stopping the water flow.
- [ ] Avoid using chemical drain cleaners regularly — why it matters: These harsh chemicals can damage your pipes over time, leading to more significant plumbing issues that make your system prone to backups.
- [ ] Be mindful of older toilets — why it matters: Older toilets, especially those not designed for water efficiency, may have weaker flushing power and be more prone to clogging, sometimes needing more frequent attention or replacement.
- [ ] Get professional drain cleaning for recurring clogs — why it matters: If you're plunging your toilet often, it's not just a toilet clog; it could be a sign of a deeper issue in your drain line or even the main sewer line that needs a professional assessment to prevent future overflows and backups.

What to Do Next
By following this checklist, you can significantly reduce the risk of an unexpected toilet overflow. If you do notice persistent issues like frequent clogs or a continuously running toilet, it's wise to call a licensed plumber.
